turns.question: Where are streaming responses implemented, and which public API methods route into the streaming implementation?
turns.text:
I'll investigate the repository structure using the gh CLI to find streaming implementation.Now I have a complete picture. Let me quickly check the realtime resource since it uses WebSockets rather than SSE, for completeness.Confirmed — Realtime uses a separate WebSocket-based mechanism (`src/realtime/websocket.ts`, `ws.ts`), distinct from the SSE `Stream` class. I now have enough to give a complete, evidence-backed answer.

## Where streaming is implemented

**Core transport (SSE parsing):** `src/core/streaming.ts`
- `export class Stream<Item> implements AsyncIterable<Item>` — wraps a `fetch` `Response`/`ReadableStream` into an async iterable of parsed JSON events.
- `Stream.fromSSEResponse()` — parses `text/event-stream` bytes into JS objects (used for Chat Completions, Responses, Completions, Assistants, image/audio streaming).
- `Stream.fromReadableStream()` — parses newline-delimited JSON (an alternate framing).
- `_iterSSEMessages()` / `SSEDecoder` / `iterSSEChunks()` — low-level line/event decoding.
- Note: `src/streaming.ts` is just a deprecated re-export (`export * from './core/streaming'`), confirming this moved from a flat layout to `src/core/` in a recent refactor.

**Dispatch point (decides streamed vs. buffered parsing):** `src/internal/parse.ts`, function `defaultParseResponse()`. It checks `props.options.stream`; if true, it calls either a custom `props.options.__streamClass.fromSSEResponse(...)` (used for typed helper streams) or falls back to the generic `Stream.fromSSEResponse(...)`. This is invoked by `src/core/api-promise.ts` (`APIPromise.parse()`), which every resource method returns.

**Higher-level ergonomic streaming helpers** (build on `Stream`, add event-emitter semantics, accumulation, and parsing):
- `src/lib/EventStream.ts` — abstract base class (`class EventStream<EventTypes>`) providing `.on()`, promises for `done()`/`finalX()`, abort handling.
- `src/lib/ChatCompletionStream.ts` — `ChatCompletionStream`, static `createChatCompletion()`, accumulates chunks into a final `ChatCompletion`.
- `src/lib/ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.ts` / `AbstractChatCompletionRunner.ts` — tool-calling runner loop for streaming.
- `src/lib/responses/ResponseStream.ts` — `ResponseStream`, static `createResponse()`, plus `src/lib/responses/ResponseAccumulator.ts` and `EventTypes.ts` for the Responses API.
- `src/lib/AssistantStream.ts` — `AssistantStream`, `createAssistantStream()` / `createToolAssistantStream()`, for the (beta) Assistants Runs API.

**Realtime is a separate mechanism**, not SSE: `src/realtime/websocket.ts` and `src/realtime/ws.ts` implement a WebSocket-based client (`src/resources/realtime.ts` just re-exports `./realtime/index`).

## Public API methods that route into streaming

Each of these resource methods sets `stream: body.stream ?? false` in the request options passed to `this._client.post/get(...)`, which flows through `APIPromise` → `defaultParseResponse` → `Stream.fromSSEResponse`:

| Method | File |
|---|---|
| `client.chat.completions.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts:69-79` |
| `client.chat.completions.stream(...)` (helper) | same file, ~line 221, delegates to `ChatCompletionStream.createChatCompletion` |
| `client.chat.completions.runTools(...)` (stream variant) | same file, ~line 190-215, delegates to `ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.runTools` |
| `client.responses.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/responses/responses.ts:96-106` |
| `client.responses.retrieve(id, {stream:true})` | same file, `retrieve()` |
| `client.responses.stream(...)` (helper) | same file, ~line 201-206, delegates to `ResponseStream.createResponse` |
| `client.completions.create({stream:true})` (legacy Completions) | `src/resources/completions.ts:41` |
| `client.images.edit/generate({stream:true})` (partial image events) | `src/resources/images.ts:58,91` |
| `client.audio.transcriptions.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/audio/transcriptions.ts:62` |
| `client.beta.threads.createAndRun({stream:true})` | `src/resources/beta/threads/threads.ts:160` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/beta/threads/runs/runs.ts:79` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.stream(...)` (helper, and deprecated `.createAndRunStream`) | same file, lines 169, 232, delegate to `AssistantStream.createAssistantStream` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.submitToolOutputs({stream:true})` / `.stream(...)` | same file, lines 263, 299, delegate to `AssistantStream.createToolAssistantStream` |

All of the above are confirmed by direct file reads via `gh api repos/openai/openai-node/contents/<path>` at ref `71d2347c...` (repo's current `main` HEAD at investigation time).

## What I did not verify
- I did not read the full bodies of `ChatCompletionStream.ts`, `ResponseStream.ts`, `AssistantStream.ts`, or `AbstractChatCompletionRunner.ts` line-by-line (only headers/imports) — internal accumulation logic details are not fully confirmed, only their entry points.
- I did not verify the WebSocket realtime implementation internals (`src/realtime/ws.ts`, `websocket.ts`) beyond confirming their existence and that `resources/realtime.ts` re-exports them.
- I did not check `src/resources/videos.ts` or `containers.ts` for streaming (not surfaced by the `stream ?? false` search pattern; likely non-streaming, but not exhaustively confirmed).
- I worked against the `main` branch HEAD at the time of the query (commit `71d2347c...`); did not check a specific release tag, so exact line numbers could shift in newer commits.
